subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw keep default steering as boundary-based behavior, or add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context?
rationale: The choice affects shared runtime semantics, user-visible channel behavior, Codex/native runtime integration, and compatibility with existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt modes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with coverage for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported default and use related work only to ensure messages reach the existing boundary-based policy.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger soft-steer lifecycle only after maintainer-approved upgrade proof and channel/runtime compatibility coverage.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with coverage for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-history signal on shared active-run steering and replacement PR work.
